description: Voronoi Diagram by Office Solution A Voronoi diagram is a way of dividing a plane into regions based on distance to a specific set of points. Each region contains all the points that are closer to one particular seed point than to any other seed point. These seed points are also known as sites or generators. Here's a breakdown of its components: Voronoi Cells: Each seed point has a corresponding region, called a Voronoi cell, which consists of all points closer to that seed than any other. Edges and Vertices: The edges of the Voronoi cells are equidistant to the nearest two seed points. The vertices are equidistant to three or more seed points. Convex Polygons: In a plane, Voronoi cells are convex polygons. Seeds: Start with a set of points (called seeds or sites). Regions: Divide the plane such that each region contains all points closer to its seed than to any other seed. Basic Features: Visual Clarity: The visual is clearly visible, and the data are easily identifiable. Size: The chart is resizable and dynamic in nature according to the size. Dynamic Data Handling: Capable of managing large datasets with ease, ensuring smooth performance and quick rendering. Colors: The colors of the dots and the separators in the chart can be changed from the visual settings under the visualization pane.
